title: Reverse proxy, load balancing and serving static files

videos.script: The bookshop answers on two ports nobody outside should ever see. Eight thousand and one, and eight thousand and two. {{ports}} A visitor knows one name and one port. Something has to stand at that door and decide where each request goes. {{door}} That is a reverse proxy. Nginx takes the request, opens a connection of its own to the shop, and hands the answer back. The visitor never learns the shop exists. {{proxy}} With two copies of the shop, the proxy also chooses which one answers. Each in turn, or the least busy, or always the same one for the same visitor. {{balance}} And when one copy stops, the proxy notices and stops sending it work. When both stop, it says so, with an error that names the problem. {{fail}} By the end of this lesson one name serves the static front and the API, from two copies of the application, with compression and sensible limits. {{end}}
